structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' with 'we' to make suggestions.
structures.example: Tomorrow evening there is Laura Pausini's concert in Turin. Shall we go? (Italian, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)

structures.can_do: Can use 'ought to have' + '-ed' to refer to desired states of affairs in the past.
structures.example: Another point, which I think ought to have been better managed, was the boat trip on the Thames. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'ought' + subject + 'not to' + verb to form (rhetorical) questions, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: And if not, ought we not to learn from the mistakes of the past? (Denmark; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Danish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form 'ought not to'.
structures.example: Secondly, there ought not to be a division between rich and poor. (Netherlands; C2 MASTERY; 1999; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: Shall we meet at half past 4 in front of my house? (Japanese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' to express commands in very formal contexts.
structures.example: We therefore need to insist that the agreement is binding and that the contract shall be fulfilled. (Swiss German, C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' in the main clause after an 'if-' clause  ► conditionals
structures.example: Nowadays people live longer than they did in the past, which is very nice and pleasant, but we must be careful because if things get out of hand, … we shall be doomed to live in complete chaos. (Portuguese, C2 MASTERY, Pass, 1993)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: You shouldn't miss it. (Thai, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' to talk about plans and intentions, particularly in formal contexts.
structures.example: I promise that I shall cover all the work and give it to you tomorrow. (Thai, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' to make predictions.
structures.example: As a result, our town shall have financial benefits, as people visiting the library will visit the city’s shops for their needs. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'shall' to seek advice.
structures.example: What shall I buy for her wedding? (Slovak, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2004)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: You should come at 6 o'clock. (Russian, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2009)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: This way, students shall not die of boredom or feel that their stay was useless. (Japan; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: Should I wear special clothes? (Farsi, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' to give advice.
structures.example: It was only €70. It is pink. It looks very nice. My advice, you should buy this. (Turkish, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should have' + '-ed'.
structures.example: I have an appointment. I know I shouldn't have taken it during school time but I had no other choice. (French, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' have + '-ed'.
structures.example: You should have been with us. (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2002)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' to make suggestions.
structures.example: I think we should meet at 2 pm, and my mother will take us there so don't worry. (Spanish - Latin American, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the question tag form 'shouldn't' + pronoun to make suggestions and ask for opinions.
structures.example: When you come back, we should rent some movies, shouldn't we? (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' to talk about what is likely to happen.
structures.example: [talking about an event] It should be a good day! (Russian; B1 THRESHOLD; Pass; 2009)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' to talk about ideal or desired situations.
structures.example: British people should eat more vegetables and fruit and avoid fast food! (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2010)

structures.can_do: Can use 'you shouldn’t have' (+ '-ed') in polite acceptance of a gift.
structures.example: Thank you for the present you sent me, you shouldn't have! (===NONE===, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2003)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' and 'shouldn't' without a following verb where the previous main verb is understood.
structures.example: Well, have you ever checked your blood pressure? I think you should. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'you should have' + '-ed' to emphasise points in a story.
structures.example: You should have heard the noise. (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2002)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should have' + '-ed' to talk about regrets or undesirable situations in the past.
structures.example: You should have been there with me, I had a great time. (Chile; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should be' + '-ing'.
structures.example: Well, you should be bouncing up and down with joy (just kidding)! (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should' after 'if' to talk about possible situations in the future.
structures.example: If you should change your mind and prefer to take a taxi, you can do it outside the airport by calling this number: 3570. (Italian, C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY, Pass, 1993)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should be' + '-ing' to talk about present general obligation.
structures.example: Wild animals should be running free but I think that zoos today have an important role in keeping them alive. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'should be' + '-ing' to talk about expectations.
Can use 'should' with an inverted subject to refer to possible situations, in formal contexts.
structures.example: Should you need any further information, don't hesitate to contact us. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'used to' to talk about repeated actions or states in the past that are no longer true.
structures.example: When I was I child, I used to go to a small school and I enjoyed it very much. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'used to' without a following verb where the previous main verb is understood. ► ellipsis
structures.example: She doesn't travel as much as she used to. (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I used to share my room with my brother. (Albania; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Albanian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: [talking about a change in eating habits] What did we use to eat? (Netherlands; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms 'didn't use to' and 'didn't used to'.
structures.example: We didn't use to talk to each other. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'as' + pronoun + 'used to' … to add background to a narrative, often to highlight something unusual.
structures.example: She had gone out for a walk in the woods as she used to do every Sunday, with her diary in her hand and a pen in her pocket. (Italy; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to ask about plans and intentions.
structures.example: Will you come by bus? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative forms.
structures.example: I will be at your house at 7.30 because I have an appointment before. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: Will you be at home? (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms.
structures.example: Don't worry, you won't need anything apart from some pencils and your art book. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to talk about willingness and offers
structures.example: My mother will get us there, and she will bring us to my house after too. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to talk about plans and intentions.
structures.example: I will bring some music to the dinner. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Bengali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative form 'used not to'
structures.example: I used to play until late in the evening, I used not to do my homework and I did not excel at school. (Italy; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' in the main clause after an 'if-' clause to talk about possible future situations. ► conditionals
structures.example: If I need a camera, I will use my mobile phone. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to make requests in a limited range of contexts.
structures.example: Will you come with me? (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Telugu; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to talk about fixed plans in the future, often with timetabled times or dates.
structures.example: Mr Miller, the Sales Director, will visit us next Thursday. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to talk about something which is typical or habitual.
structures.example: The abundance of ingredients required in any recipe will result normally in a spicy but nutritious dish, a dish that will usually contain some kind of sauce made of hot pepper, tomatoes, garlic and onion, some kind of meat and also some vegetables. (Mexico; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to talk about general behaviour, often disapprovingly.
structures.example: Indeed no one can imagine what children will do! (France; C2 MASTERY; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' to make predictions.► question tags
structures.example: I think that in 20 years' time it will be bigger than it is, because my town is growing very fast. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'will' (particularly 'Will you please') to make requests and commands in a wide range of contexts.
structures.example: Will you please send me his name, address and telephone number. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would like to invite' to make invitations.
structures.example: I would like to invite you to dinner in my house on Saturday at 7 30 pm. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Others; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with 'like'.
structures.example: I'd like to invite you to dinner. (Farsi, A1 BREAKTHROUGH, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would like' to talk about wishes and preferences.
structures.example: If possible, I'd like to come to see you on Tuesday afternoon. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms.
structures.example: [talking about clothes] You wouldn't believe how much they cost! (Chinese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I'd love to have a pen-friend in Japan. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' with a wide range of verbs to talk about wishes and preferences.
structures.example: I would prefer to go on Sunday, because on Sunday I have no school. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'it would be' to make suggestions.
structures.example: [talking about a jazz concert] It would be very good if you came with me. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Oriya; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would not have' + '-ed' or 'wouldn’t have' + '-ed'
structures.example: Without your help, I wouldn't have got this result. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would have' + '-ed'.
structures.example: I did not think my friend Janis would have done that. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' to talk about imagined situations.
structures.example: I was thinking of painting my bedroom blue. It would look awesome. (Bengali, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form 'would you like'.
structures.example: Sarah, would you like to play tennis this evening? (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' in the main clause of a conditional sentence to talk about an imagined situation, often in the context of advice or opinion-giving.
structures.example: It's your decision but if I had the chance, I would go with my friends. (German, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' to talk about the future in the past.
structures.example: I've just bought a new dress, and a beautiful black T-shirt. When I saw them, I thought they would be great for tonight's party. (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2010)

structures.can_do: Can use an limited range of adverbs with 'would', including 'really', 'probably', 'certainly', 'definitely'.► adverbs
structures.example: I hope you will come soon, and I think that you would really enjoy it because is something different of what you are used to. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use question forms.
structures.example: Would you let me know what you think? (French, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2011)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' to make polite requests, often in the fixed expression 'would you mind'.
structures.example: Would you tell me about your room in your next letter, please? (Chinese, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2001)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' to talk about habitual actions and events in the past.
structures.example: [talking about a job that the speaker did last year] In my opinion I worked very hard. I would spend a lot of hours at work. (Chinese, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 2011)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' with verbs such as 'advise', 'imagine', 'recommend', 'say' to be less direct.
structures.example: I'd advise you to go with your friends because I bet you'll have so much fun! (German, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.guideword: USE: IMAGINED SITUATIONS IN THE PAST
structures.can_do: Can use 'would' to talk about imagined situations in the past. ► conditionals
structures.example: The next week I would have flown to Miami to meet George Clooney. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would' as the past form of 'will' in reported clauses.
structures.example: She accepted the invitation and she said that she would come on the 21st of June. (Spanish - European, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms of 'would' to talk about willingness in the past.
structures.example: We had to leave without you because the bus driver wouldn't wait. (===NONE===, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2004)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of adverbs with 'would', including 'strongly', 'easily', 'especially', 'actually', 'absolutely', 'gladly'  ► adverbs
structures.example: Considering the aspects of our education system, and the results of my research, I would strongly recommend the following changes to be made. (Croatia; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Croatian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of adverbs with 'would', including 'undoubtedly', 'possibly', 'normally', 'personally', 'eventually', 'obviously', 'significantly', 'inevitably'. ► adverbs
structures.example: [talking about the construction of a leisure centre] I believe that the construction of such a centre would undoubtedly contribute to the improvement of our quality of life. (Greek, C2 MASTERY, Pass, 2009)

structures.can_do: Can use adverbs of certainty and possibility ('maybe', 'perhaps'), before a clause or ellipted clause. ► adverbs: position
structures.example: I think I left my phone there, maybe in your kitchen. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: MID POSITION, HEDGING OR EMPHASIS
structures.can_do: Can use adverbs in mid position or after main verb 'be', to modify an assertion, either through hedging or emphasis. ► adverbs: position
structures.example: It is probably in the sitting room on the table. (Czech Republic; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Czech; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of adverbs, for emphasis.
structures.example: If I were you I'd certainly choose not to go with your parents. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use adverbs expressing certainty as short responses.
structures.example: Do I agree with this statement? Definitely. (Russia; C2 MASTERY; 2000; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'not necessarily' as a short response.
structures.example: Presents. Strips, bows, paper-wrapping. Thinking of Christmas? Not necessarily. (Portugal; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: MODAL VERB + MODAL ADVERB, HEDGING OR EMPHASIS
structures.can_do: Can use modal verb + modal adverb to modify an assertion, either through hedging or emphasis.
structures.example: Next year you can surely go somewhere with your friends. (Portugal; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'not necessarily' to express a possible exception to a general perception, i.e. not in every case.
structures.example: As a conclusion, I want to say that while what we wear doesn't necessarily define who we are, it does play a big part in it. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' + subject + 'possibly' to make requests more polite.
structures.example: Could I possibly see you at 3.30? (Thailand; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Thai; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' to make requests.
structures.example: Could you help me to paint my bedroom? (Portuguese, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form of 'could' to talk about inability.
structures.example: [talking about the key to an office] I couldn't work without it. (Germany; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: You could come by bus, and we could meet at the bus station. (Spanish - European, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2010)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form of 'could' to talk about ability.
structures.example: … she could hear a man talking, he was giving her orders… (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: Could you help me? (Polish, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: [talking about a party] Too bad you couldn't come. (Somali, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2004)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' with a limited range of verbs to make suggestions.
structures.example: We could have dinner after that, if you want. (Egypt; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Arabic - Egyptian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could I' to seek permission.
structures.example: I am in the basketball team of my school and tomorrow there is an important game. Could I take the class that I will miss on Saturday? (Spanish - Latin American, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2006)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' to talk about possibility.
structures.example: But believe me, it could be really fun to have a talkative person as your friend, he or she will give you good laugh at anytime! (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' with an increasing range of verbs to make suggestions.
structures.example: …you could become a member of a gym. (Greek, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2009)

structures.can_do: Can used 'could' have + '-ed'.
structures.example: In fact it could have been dangerous but it became funny and also an embarrassing moment in my life! (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' form to express disapproval or criticism.
structures.example: Since your travel company chose a hotel that far from the city, I think that you could have arranged entertainment at the hotel. (Swedish, C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY, Pass, 1998)

structures.can_do: Can used affirmative 'could' have + '-ed' to talk about past possibility.
structures.example: Alice was disappointed that her mother could have phoned her but she did not. (Japan; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' to talk about regrets.
structures.example: I wish I could have stayed, especially to help the children. (Spanish - Latin American, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could have' + '-ed' to speculate about the past.
structures.example: I thought perhaps a thief could have entered my house. (Italian, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993)

structures.can_do: Can use 'could' as the past form of 'can' in reported speech.
structures.example: I told them I couldn't go because I didn't have money, I wasn't honest! (Spanish - European, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1999)

structures.can_do: Can use 'couldn’t have' + '-ed' to speculate about the past.
structures.example: Imagine my dismay when I realised I hadn’t brought back the notebook from the pub. Surely I couldn't have left it on my seat. (French, C2 MASTERY, Pass, 1993)

structures.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the present simple with 'don't' + main verb. ► present simple ► can
structures.example: I don't have a dining room, so we eat in the living room. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Romanian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verb 'be', with contracted and uncontracted forms.
structures.example: My college is not very big. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of determiners as pronouns and indefinite pronouns in negative contexts.  ► Pronouns: quantity
structures.example: I bought a shirt, because I haven't got any. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative forms of modal verbs. ► modal verbs
structures.example: I'm sorry I can't come to your wedding because I am very sick. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative imperatives of main verbs with 'don’t' + main verb. ► Clauses: imperatives
structures.example: Don't forget your electric guitar. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the present continuous and present perfect with 'be' and 'have' + 'not/n't'.  ► present continuous ► present perfect
structures.example: The gas is not working. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Gujarati; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative form 'can’t'.
structures.example: In winter, we can't go visiting because it is too cold. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Nepali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the past simple with 'didn’t' + main verb. ► past simple
structures.example: It was very sad that you didn't come to my birthday party but it's ok. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Hindi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative statements of main verbs in the past continuous and past perfect with auxiliary verbs 'be' and 'have' + 'not/n't'. ► past continuous ► past perfect
structures.example: It was raining for seventy two hours and it wasn't going to stop. (Ukraine; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative question forms in main clauses and question tags. ► questions
structures.example: Can't you go with your parents some time and with your friends later? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms of mental process verbs ('I don’t think', 'I don’t believe') followed by a complement clause, where the negative form is in the mental process verb rather than the complement clause.
structures.example: But I don't think it'll help you. (Kazakhstan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Kazakh; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use determiners 'any', 'much' and 'many' with nouns in negative contexts. ► Determiners: quantity
structures.example: I bought them because I didn't have any shirts or hats. (Portugal; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use determiner 'no' with nouns.  ► Determiners: quantity
structures.example: I bought these clothes because I need them for my new job, but now I have no money because they cost £250. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: 'NOT', NON FINITE AND ELLIPTED CLAUSES
structures.can_do: Can use 'not' before a non-finite or ellipted clause.
structures.example: But every time a small envelope arrived, I ripped it open as fast as I could. Not this time. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use uncontracted 'not' for emphasis or in formal contexts.
structures.example: Do not take on too many assignments at a time. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative questions and question tags to involve the listener/reader by seeking agreement or checking something.
structures.example: Isn't it marvellous? (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns in negative contexts.
structures.example: I said I had nothing, but he didn't believe me. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use adverbs 'ever', 'never', 'yet', 'still' in negative contexts.
structures.example: Nobody will ever know who that man was. (Chile; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'whatsoever' after a negative form for emphasis.
structures.example: This means that nothing shall change for the employees, there shall be no implication whatsoever for their rights stipulated in their employment contracts. (Czech Republic; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2007; Czech; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'do' + inverted subject after 'not only', to give focus.
structures.example: Not only was it in a wonderful location, with extraordinary views, but it was also very accessible and the shops were really near. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'not' + stance adverb, often  in a mid position, to soften the directness of a statement.
structures.example: This is not necessarily the way the older generation would see it, though. (Slovenia; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Slovene; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative pronoun 'none' to substitute for subject and object pronouns or noun phrases. ► pronouns: substitution
structures.example: In fact, there are none, but the hills that do exist can be dubbed mountains - just because there are none... (Russia; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative forms 'neither of' and 'none of' + pronoun or noun phrase with the affirmative form of the verb.
structures.example: Neither of us is liable in this case. (Czech Republic; B2 VANTAGE; 2007; Slovak; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'neither … nor' to connect two words, phrases or clauses, often to give emphasis or focus.
structures.example: Neither you nor I would like that. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'not with indefinite pronouns 'everyone' and 'everything' and determiners 'every', 'all'.
structures.example: Not everyone likes sports or music. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use '(very) few' meaning 'not many' to refer to people in formal written contexts, often reports or surveys.
structures.example: They were sent to Britain to improve their English but few had any real contact with the language. (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'never' in front position followed by an inverted subject (most commonly 'I') + main verb, to give focus.
structures.example: Never have I seen such a realistic and impressive film before. (Argentina; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'not a' + noun, often with a following  passive structure, for emphasis.
structures.example: Not a single noise could be heard from inside of any of the rooms. (Argentina; C2 MASTERY; 2000; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a negative imperative form with 'you' to give a warning or reprimand.
structures.example: Don't you ever do that again! (Cyprus; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'Neither' or 'Nor' + with 'do' or 'be' + inverted subject to add to a previous related negative clause, to focus on an additional negative factor.
structures.example: There are also considerable disturbances during day-time. It is, for example, not possible to lead a conversation, e.g. on the veranda, without shouting. Nor is it possible to watch television peacefully without the thunderous noise in the background. (Germany; C2 MASTERY; 1993; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'in the least' after a negative form for emphasis.
structures.example: She has lost her little brother but that does not discourage her in the least. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying plural nouns with an adjective and no determiner.
structures.example: I have new neighbours. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Gujarati; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying singular and plural nouns with an adjective after a determiner.
structures.example: Martin is my best friend. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Slovak; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + singular and plural nouns. ► Nouns and noun phrases: functions
structures.example: There is also a park near my house. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Pashto; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases by pre-modifying a limited range of nouns with another noun.
structures.example: Every Friday I go swimming and play computer games. (Poland; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Polish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS POSTMODIFIER
structures.can_do: Can post-modify noun phrases by using a non-defining relative clause. ► Clauses: relative
structures.example: She's in a volleyball team like me, but we're not in the same one. She was for the other team, which lost. (Switzerland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form simple noun phrases by pre-modifying nouns with an increasing range of determiners.
structures.example: There are so many shops, you can play games, eat food like Chinese food. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form simple noun phrases with a limited range of determiners + uncountable nouns.
structures.example: The food was delicious and the music was great. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can pre-modify noun phrases with a limited range of more than one adjective.
structures.example: I bought a beautiful pink skirt and a white top. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADVERBS + ADJECTIVES
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases with adverb + adjective + noun.
structures.example: It took us a very long time but it was a great fun! (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases by using a prepositional phrase after the main noun in a noun phrase.
structures.example: It was a beautiful red dress with blue flowers on the back. (Andorra; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; French; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE AS COMPLEMENT
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases by using a defining relative clause as a complement to a noun phrase. ► Clauses: relative
structures.example: The mobile phone which I bought yesterday is brilliant. (Russia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Russian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADJECTIVES
structures.can_do: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with more than one adjective.
structures.example: The Northeast is so beautiful and it's famous because of its white sandy beaches and the coconut trees. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use possessive determiner ''s' with a singular noun.
structures.example: It's my sister's jacket. (Uruguay; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with 'such a' + adjective + singular noun and 'such' + adjective + plural noun, to give emphasis.
structures.example: It was so terrible because I've never been in such a terrible situation. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a clause with a present perfect or past perfect as a superlative noun phrase complement, to talk about uniqueness.
structures.example: It has the best promenade I have seen. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can omit the noun after possessive '’s' to talk about a place which is familiar to the speaker and listener.
structures.example: Last week I left my clothes at the dry cleaner's and I can't collect them. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can put two noun phrases together (in apposition) to refer to the same person or thing, usually separated by commas.
structures.example: Mr Miller, the Sales Director, will visit us next Thursday. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the noun phrase 'The thing' in front position, with a clause complement, to give focus to something.
structures.example: The thing I enjoyed most about it was a new computer game. (Georgia (Republic of); B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Georgian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with plural nouns + ' + noun.
structures.example: He had promised that he would go to his grandparents' house this afternoon. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE '‘S' + NOUN
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases with noun phrase + 'of' + noun phrase + possessive determiner ''s' + noun phrase.
structures.example: I ran to the street and I saw the window of my neighbour's car was broken. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with an indefinite pronoun + adjective or clause.
structures.example: We see each other every day and do something different every day. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; ; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with noun + 'of' + possessive determiner + noun + '‘s', particularly with 'friend' or 'friends'.
structures.example: Actually, I know a great one and they can make a little discount for us because the owner is a friend of my father's. (Albania; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Albanian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with 'a friend of' or 'friends of' + possessive determiner + noun.
structures.example: He is a friend of my husband. (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form noun phrases with noun + 'of' + possessive pronouns.
structures.example: … we always did everything together and couldn't stop laughing as she told me many funny stories and I told her lots of silly mistakes of mine. (Vietnam; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases by using adjective phrases as postmodifiers to give more information about the noun.
structures.example: Besides, we could leave one day in the morning and go by boat to a small and exotic island full of different and exotic species of birds that we could observe and photograph. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: NOUN PHRASE WITH POSSESSIVE 'S WITHOUT NOUN
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases with noun phrase + 'of' + noun phrase + possessive determiner ''s', omitting the noun where it is previously mentioned.
structures.example: Our after-sales team now is perceived as faster, more qualified, friendlier and more efficient than our competitors’. (China; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH ADJECTIVES COMBINED WITH 'BUT'
structures.can_do: Can form an increasing range of complex noun phrases with more than one adjective combined with 'but'.
structures.example: I am very lucky, because I was born in a small but beautiful city called Neuva Helvecia. (Uruguay; B2 VANTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use nominalised forms in academic or business contexts, to make something more formal.
structures.example: As indicated by the charts, the output in state-owned industry increased by 12% in 2000. (Poland; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use proper nouns with a capital letter to refer to specific people, places, days and things.
structures.example: I want to see you on Saturday and Sunday. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of common nouns.
structures.example: My house is in Ilford. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: COMPLEX NOUN PHRASES WITH 'LITTLE OR NO'  + NOUN
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases with 'little or no' + noun.
structures.example: Harvey Keitel has always chosen the scripts that interested him as a person and as an actor, whilst refusing to invest his talent in big-time Hollywood block-busters with little or no artistic value. (Italy; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases with 'wh-' cleft clauses, followed by 'be', to give focus.
structures.example: What everyone loved were the special effects and we were very impressed by the use of advanced technological innovations. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a range of compound nouns, as one-word, two-word and hyphenated compounds, formed from verb + noun, noun + noun and adjective + noun combinations.
structures.example: She likes to go to the swimming pool and to the gym. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Ukrainian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the '-ing' forms of verbs as nouns, in object position, to refer to activities.
structures.example: There we did a lot of things like swimming from the beach and going shopping. (Uruguay; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the '-ing' form of verbs as abstract nouns.
structures.example: Learning English has its rewards too. (Brazil; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form plurals of countable nouns ending in a consonant plus '-y', by changing the 'y' to 'I' and adding '-es'.
structures.example: I have a lot of hobbies. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the '-ing' form of verbs as nouns in subject position.
structures.example: Working until midnight every evening is not reasonable. Working late is not the solution and it is even dangerous. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form plurals by adding '-es' to countable nouns ending in '-o', '-ch', '-s', '-sh', '-x' or '-z'.
structures.example: The art classes after school are on Tuesdays. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form plurals by adding '-s' to common countable nouns.
structures.example: We play computer games. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of common nouns.
structures.example: When you're swimming you exercise all of your body. (2649025_2; PET; Cyprus; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form some irregular plural nouns.
structures.example: It was a sale and I bought some clothes for my children. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Somali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use collective nouns, usually with a singular verb, but also with a plural verb depending on whether the noun is perceived as a single group or collection of individuals.
structures.example: The staff is friendly and polite with guests and there are many sports activities. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of uncountable nouns.
structures.example: I listen to music, I watch TV and I talk to my friends. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2000; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: NOUNS ONLY USED IN THE PLURAL
structures.can_do: Can use nouns that only have a plural form, with plural agreement.
structures.example: I bought them because I feel comfortable when I am wearing these clothes. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Malay; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use uncountable nouns with 'the' to talk about something specific.
structures.example: The music is going to be loud, since it's rap. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use uncountable nouns with an increasing range of quantity words and phrases including 'much', 'a bit of', 'a little bit of', 'enough', 'further', 'plenty of', 'loads of'.  ►  Determiners: quantity
structures.example: I'm sure that your parents are looking forward to going with you to the beach, because they work a lot of hours during the year so they can't spend much time with you. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of uncountable nouns, particularly referring to abstract concepts.
structures.example: I appreciate that your company is concerned about safety and has installed safety belts in every coach but they do not help much when they are all broken. (Denmark; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Danish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use uncountable nouns with a limited range of quantity words and phrases including 'some', 'any', 'a lot of', 'more'. ► Determiners: quantity
structures.example: It's really important for me, because I need to do some homework. (Czech Republic; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Czech; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can refer to an individual example or quantity of an uncountable noun using words for containers and countable items.
structures.example: We have to bring a bottle of water, trainers and a T-shirt or top. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use nouns and noun phrases as subjects of the clause.
structures.example: His name is Stanislav. (Singhalese, A1 BREAKTHROUGH)

structures.can_do: Can use uncountable nouns without a definite article to refer to an abstract thing in general.
structures.example: Television is more attractive because it has moving images. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of uncountable nouns.
structures.example: I think the countryside is better than the town centre, people get on more easily with each other. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Other; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of prepositions in prepositional phrases.
structures.example: I invite you and your family to come to my house for dinner. (Portuguese, A1 BREAKTHROUGH)

structures.can_do: Can use nouns and noun phrases as objects of the clause.
structures.example: I love my house. (Thai, A1 BREAKTHROUGH)

structures.can_do: Can use nouns and noun phrases as adjuncts in some time expressions.
structures.example: But if not, then I will see you tomorrow morning. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use nouns and noun phrases as complements of the verb 'be'.
structures.example: There is a big garden. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Urdu; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: WITH 'BY' IN A RELATIVE CLAUSE|
structures.can_do: Can use the passive with 'by' in a relative clause, often to add more information.
structures.example: I also like wearing clothes which are manufactured by famous brands. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Tamil; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple passive affirmative after a singular subject.
structures.example: It was built in 1880. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple passive affirmative with a singular subject.
structures.example: The group is called "playmo". (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with 'by' to add information about something already known.
structures.example: It was bought by my uncle. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.
structures.example: Our office is situated near the airport. (B1 Argentina ; Spanish - Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple passive affirmative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects both singular and plural.
structures.example: It was written in a strange language that I tried to translate. (B1 Spanish - Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous passive affirmative with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: Did you know that the next Harry Potter movie is being filmed in my school? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive infinitive after a limited number of forms including 'going to', 'have to', 'need to', 'want to'.
structures.example: It is going to be shown this Friday. (B1 PET Turkish)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive infinitive affirmative and negative forms after an increasing range of main verbs, modal verbs, adjectives and nouns, in impersonal constructions.
structures.example: According to your advertisement, some training is supposed to be given. (B2 South Korean)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous passive to refer to the future.
structures.example: The seminar is being held at Chennai in the next week. (India; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Marathi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect passive affirmative form.
structures.example: The car had been serviced and everything seemed to be all right. (B2 Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple affirmative and negative forms with modal verbs to refer to the past.
structures.example: I think that all these problems could have been avoided and that asking for my money back is the best way of forgetting that evening. (B2 Catalan)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with 'by' to give focus.
structures.example: My school was chosen by the TV company because it is one of the newest in town. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS.
structures.can_do: Can use the past simple passive with a limited range of verbs needing two objects, putting the indirect object in subject position.
structures.example: So I was given a ticket for a train, running from Berlin to Munich. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple passive negative with a range of pronoun and noun subjects.
structures.example: The story is about a girl, who is not accepted in her class. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous passive affirmative.
structures.example: However, to my disappointment, the restaurant was closed because it was being redecorated. (B2 Chinese)

structures.can_do: Can use past simple passive negative.
structures.example: What is worse, the ticket price was not reduced despite the fact that I showed my student ID. (B2 Japanese)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect passive negative form.
structures.example: [talking about a car] In fact, it hadn't been stolen, it had been taken by a man and his wife, because their car broke down and because she was about to have her baby … (B2 Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous passive affirmative with an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: This year's topic is the online training for employees, which is being relaunched . (2786698_1; BECV; Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 2010; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous passive negative.
structures.example: … students are not being educated equally. (Mongolia; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Mongolian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a passive non-finite '-ing' form as a subordinate clause or a noun clause to give explanatory background information.
structures.example: Being born and raised in Mexico, I believe her to be this country's best representative to the world. (C1 Spanish - Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect passive affirmative form (often in the context of reporting).  ► reported speech
structures.example: I have been asked to write a report about an accident which happened to me last Saturday. (B2 Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with modal verbs to evaluate or summarise.
structures.example: In conclusion, it can be seen that the bicycle is more suitable for those who are living in a little town or in the country. (B2 Italian)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS, , WITH PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE
structures.can_do: Can use the passive with a range of tenses and verbs needing two objects (e.g. give, offer, sell) with the direct object in subject position and the indirect object in a prepositional phrase.
structures.example: Your name was given to me by a member of yours, Allan Westwood, whom I met last week. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with 'will' to talk about the future.
structures.example: Just to let you know you will be booked into the Palace Hotel … (B2 Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with modal verbs in a range of contexts, with a variety of subjects.
structures.example: Architects should be hired to design parks, where people could go for a walk or have a picnic. (B2 Polish)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH VERBS TAKING TWO OBJECTS.
structures.can_do: Can use the passive with a wide range of verbs needing two objects, putting the indirect object in subject position.
structures.example: I was very happy to hear that you have been offered two jobs, one in a restaurant and one in a museum. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect passive negative form (often in the context of reporting). ► reported speech
structures.example: …the old-fashioned house which has not been used for twenty years is not a very attractive sight from our town either. (B2 Danish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous passive negative form to refer to ongoing situations in the present.
structures.example: In my opinion, the store is not being promoted enough. (C1 Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use passive non-finite '-ing' perfect forms in subordinate clauses to give explanatory background information.
structures.example: I myself, having been educated the hard way, would specifically insist on them getting the best possible school education. (C2 German)

structures.can_do: Can use non-finite '-ing' perfect forms of the passive as the complement of prepositions.
structures.example: They are expected to give the couple expensive presents as a reward for having been invited. (C2 Spanish - Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the passive with 'it' as a dummy subject, to summarise or evaluate in discussions, usually in formal or academic writing.
structures.example: To sum up, it can be concluded that this report has attempted to summarize the main points regarding the Spanish educational system. (C1  Spanish - European)

structures.can_do: Can form the 'get'-passive with a range of forms of 'get' + past participles.
structures.example: [talking about a mirror] I bought it because mine got broken, so I need it to see myself in it. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use have + object + -ed to talk about something where the speaker is in a pro-active or a passive role.
structures.example: After I left you on Monday, I had my car serviced and visited Washington with its wonderful memorials. (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'get' + object + '-ed' to talk about causing or instructing something to happen or to be done by somebody else, often informally.
structures.example: I must say that Caroline and I are good together because I think I am a little bit lazy but she is always the one who tries to get things done . (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a reflexive pronoun with the 'get'-passive.
structures.example: Although to drive a car you must be very careful because you could get yourself killed if you don't drive carefully enough. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'get' + object + 'to'-infinitive to talk about causing someone to do something.
structures.example: I would like to point at a few things about our small town, which I, as a citizen, have to explain to our friends, in order to get them to visit us more frequently. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'get' + object + '-ing' to talk about causing someone or something to do something.
structures.example: First of all, I would like to underline the sheer boredom of these CDs, which got me yawning from the very first minute. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'have' + object + infinitive without 'to' to talk about asking or causing someone to do something, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: In order to attract people and have them practise their English, we could point out the benefits and the possibilities one obtains, by acquiring a degree in this language ... (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2010; Greek; at level)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I was waiting for you all Saturday evening. (Spanish - European, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2004)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: Was my mother going to die? (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous with a limited range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: I was just watching a football match. (Bengali, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous to show that an event was happening in the background to the main event.
structures.example: Yesterday we were studying maths in your house, and I left my book on your bed. (Spanish - Latin American, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2005)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous with an increasing range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: He was still waiting at the traffic light. (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous to talk about actions and states in progress around a particular time in the past.
structures.example: I went to a soccer game, they were playing the last game to get the championship. (Spanish - Latin American, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous to give a reason for something, often with 'because'.
structures.example: Because she was sitting in the corner, she could see the whole view of the café in front of her. (Arabic - Meghreb, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2008)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: He was not planning to become a professional player. (Spanish - Latin American, C2 MASTERY, Pass, 2004)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous with 'always' or 'constantly' to talk about repeated events which are undesired or uncontrolled.
structures.example: They had been told that I was always getting into mischief and so had decided that, by buying me this diary, I would probably calm down a little and my behaviour would change. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous with a wide range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: My younger brother was constantly bothering me. (Russian, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1997)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous to talk about ongoing repeated events in the past, often with 'always'.
structures.example: Worst of all, in September it was always raining. (Portugal; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous to make a request or suggestions more polite or less direct.
structures.example: I was wondering if I could impose on you again for my next visit. (Chinese, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1999)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: Laura realised that she had not been studying very hard lately. (Malaysia; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous talk about a background action or event which began before a point in the past and was still continuing up to a point in the past when the main event happened.
structures.example: I had been waiting for this letter for months, so I opened it immediately. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: BACKGROUND INFORMATION WITH TIME CONJUNCTION
structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous after a time conjunction to give background information.
structures.example: After we had been sunbathing at the beach all day long, we went every evening to a cosy restaurant called "The Barking Cat", where we had a good meal and some wine. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I had been working on the project for over a year. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; French; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: BACKGROUND INFORMATION WITH RELATIVE CLAUSE
structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous in a relative clause to give background information.  ► relative clauses
structures.example: And there were two men who had been chasing the murderer to find out who the man is and rescue the girl.... (Korea, North; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Korean; Pass)

structures.guideword: USE: CONTINUING EVENTS IN THE PAST
structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous to talk about an action or event which began before a point in the past and was still continuing up to that point, often with 'for' or 'since', to give background information.
structures.example: I know it very well because we had been exchanging letters for a long time. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous to talk about events which started before a time in the past and which finished, but where the effects or results were still important at a point in the past.
structures.example: Unfortunately it had been snowing for a long time and so I was unable to go out for a walk. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative forms.
structures.example: The ABC Company called this morning to say that our company had not delivered the goods on time. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I felt really sorry for you after I had read your last letter. (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple with a limited range of adverbs (including 'never', 'ever', 'just', 'always', 'already') in the normal mid-position. ► adverbs
structures.example: It was the most beautiful one I had ever seen. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect continuous with adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: I had been working hard at my job and I had really been looking forward to this holiday. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form.
structures.example: What had he been doing that morning? (France; C2 MASTERY; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple in 'if'-clauses to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret. ► 'if'-clauses
structures.example: If the weather had been better, we would have enjoyed it more. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple after 'because' to give explanatory information.
structures.example: He was sleeping but I realised that this was because he had lost a lot of blood. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: AFTER 'IF ONLY' AND 'WISH', IMAGINED PAST
structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form after 'if only', and the affirmative and negative forms after 'wish' to talk about regret.
structures.example: If only I had listened to my father! (Iran; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Farsi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple to talk about a time before another time in the past.
structures.example: He then thought how stupid he had been. (Peru; B1; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple with a wide range of adverbs (including 'finally', 'recently', 'simply') in the normal mid-position.  ► adverbs
structures.example: He had finally achieved his goal! (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can invert the subject and auxiliary verb with 'no sooner … than' to talk about something that happened immediately before something else, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: … but no sooner had I gone to bed than someone broke the door down. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use question forms.
structures.example: Had I made the same mistake twice? (B2; 1993; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can invert the subject and auxiliary verb after 'never (before)' to talk about a unique event, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: Never had I been in such a ridiculous situation! (South Africa; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can leave out the subject before the past perfect simple where it is understood from the previous clause.
structures.example: But now she felt stronger and had lost her fear. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French)

structures.can_do: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb to talk about imagined situations in the past, often with regret, in formal contexts.
structures.example: Had I known the tour would be so bad, I wouldn't have booked it. (France; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple to report statements, where the main verb in the reporting clause is in the past simple.  ► reported speech
structures.example: […] one morning she was listening to the radio, when suddenly the announcer said that the police had arrested a man who had stolen five expensive and unique paintings. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2006; Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple to talk about situations which changed.
structures.example: After the show we had planned to go to the theatre restaurant. But it was closed. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple in relative clauses to give background information.    ► relative clauses
structures.example: After a while Mr and Mrs Landsbury, the couple who had organised the party, got everybody's attention and […] asked everybody to stay calm. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use the past perfect simple to report questions, where the main verb in the reporting clause is in the past simple.  ► reported speech
structures.example: I asked him who had given him my phone number and he said it had been me. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Polish)

structures.guideword: FORM: FIXED EXPRESSIONS 'HAD IT NOT BEEN FOR', 'IF IT HADN'T BEEN FOR'
structures.can_do: Can use 'had it not been for' … and 'if it hadn’t been for' with a modal form for giving reasons.
structures.example: Had it not been for the fact that I had already read the article, I would have thought that this woman was at least thirty years old. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form after 'if only' to express regret.
structures.example: If only she had not changed, if only I had helped her, maybe we would still be best friends and I would not be sitting here, writing about her! (Portugal; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: I forgot to tell you some details about tomorrow evening. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'you' with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: Did you buy something yesterday? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: Every day at college I went to class at 9 am. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb with 'hardly … when' to talk about something that happened immediately before something else, in formal contexts.
structures.example: Hardly had she spoken these words when it dawned on the musician that life could not continue like that. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple to talk about everyday events or states.
structures.example: The people were very polite. (A1, French)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: The player from China did not look very happy though. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with a wide range of verbs.
structures.example: I convinced some of my friends to come with me even if they don't like rap music. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'when' + past simple in subordinate clauses.
structures.example: When I arrived, the weather was horrible. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no', 'wh-', tag and negative question forms with an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: Are you still looking for a job or did you succeed in finding one? (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: I didn't realise I had lost the ring till I was at home. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple to talk about habitual states or actions.
structures.example: … he always seemed so confident to me! (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with a wide range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: I didn't hesitate and went there straight away. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple with a range of subordinating conjunctions, including 'as soon as', 'before', 'if', 'once', 'since', 'so', 'until', 'when', 'while'.
structures.example: … as soon as we went down to around 15 metres in depth, we saw a lot of coloured fish. (B2, French)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple to order sequences of events in the past, in the context of narratives.
structures.example: I remember her as a shy girl, but I read she became a manager, she went on lots of trips, she met a lot of new friends, she got married and then she got divorced. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple with 'wish (that)' to express regret that things are not different.
structures.example: I wish that you were here, cycling with us. (B1, Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple after 'if' to talk about the possible result of an imagined situation in the present or future.
structures.example: It would be better if you spent some time in the fresh air with your friends or walking in a park. (B1, Russian)

structures.can_do: Can use a range of time adjuncts with the past simple.
structures.example: I also worked as a helper on a summer camp for primary schoolchildren in Canada last summer. (B2, Japanese)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no', 'wh-', tag and negative question forms with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: Did you receive my present? (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: INVERSION WITH 'NOT ONLY … BUT ALSO'
structures.can_do: Can use the inverted form of the past simple with auxiliary 'do', in the phrase 'not only … but also'.
structures.example: The companies I found at the trade fair were very varied. Not only did I find high-technology companies, but also shoemakers, advertisement companies and plane manufacturers to name but a few. (United Kingdom; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple with 'I wondered' and 'I wanted' as politeness structures, when making polite requests and thanking.
structures.example: So, I wondered if you could introduce me to somebody who knows how to use a camera, so that I will be able to record my trip for you. (B2, Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple with 'did' for emphasis.
structures.example: We did reach the target figure and we have sent about 85 percent of the money to the hospital. (C1, Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no', 'wh-', tag and negative question forms with a wide range of verbs.  ► Questions
structures.example: Did you spot the fact that what is expected from us in Tall Trees Campsite is to help in organising the entertainment? (Sri Lanka; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Singhalese; Pass)

structures.guideword: USE: COMPLEX ORDERING OF PAST EVENTS
structures.can_do: Can use the past simple to order sequences of events in the past in a complex way.
structures.example: Following advice from a friend, I purchased the English version of your product, only to find out its quality did not match the promises made in your advertisement. (C1, Spanish - European)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple after 'if' as a politeness structure, especially in letters and emails.
structures.example: I think it would be very helpful if I told you my own case. (B2, Spanish – European)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: Have you been thinking about it a lot?! (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect continuous to talk about repeated activities which began in the past and are still continuing.
structures.example: I've been watching TV a lot, specially the sports programmes. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I have been thinking about your letter. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past simple 'I thought' as a politeness structure to sound less direct.
structures.example: I understand you are quite concerned about the matter and I thought it would be a good idea to let you know what is really going on. (C1, Spanish – Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with 'yet' to talk about events which are expected to be completed at some point in the future.
structures.example: [talking about a new mobile phone] I haven't seen it yet . (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with 'for' to talk about a past event or action which hasn't occurred again in the period of time up to now.
structures.example: I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time. (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect continuous with adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: I have just been reading an article in your newspaper this morning, about The Westfield Music Festival. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can invert the subject and affirmative auxiliary verb with 'not only … but' as a focusing device. ► focus ► inversion
structures.example: Not only have I been wandering its streets ever since I was ten, but I have also come to know most of the main characters of its history in the past 50 years. (Spain; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form 'have' + '-ed' with pronouns 'I' and 'we', and with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: I have seen the Eiffel Tower and many old buildings. (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form 'haven't' + '-ed' with 'I' with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: I haven't eaten Italian food for a long time. (Ecuador; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect continuous to talk about a single activity or state that began in the past and is still continuing, often with 'for' or 'since'.
structures.example: I've been studying International business there for four years. (Algeria; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Arabic - Meghreb; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: I hope that I have not been wasting your time and giving you too much trouble. (Malaysia; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect continuous to focus on a finished activity in the recent past but where the effects or results are still important or relevant.
structures.example: They might be slippery when it has been snowing. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form 'have you' + '-ed' with with a limited range of verbs.
structures.example: Have you bought anything? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple with 'already' to emphasise that something is done, often before the expected time.  ► adverbs
structures.example: I've already planned the party, bought his present, and most important of all, I 've already told everyone. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative forms with a range of pronouns and nouns and an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: I've left some clothes at the dry cleaner's 100 yards from my home, in Park Street. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Mandarin; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple with a limited range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: I have never seen a competition like that before, and I love it. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative forms with a range of pronouns and an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: He hasn't spoken to anyone from that time till now. (Iran; B1 THRESHOLD; 2004; Farsi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple with 'since' to talk about duration.
