structures.can_do: Can use the negative question form.
structures.example: Haven't you seen it yet? (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple to talk about experiences up to now.
structures.example: I've seen the British Museum. (Taiwan; A2 WAYSTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple to refer to a finished event or state in the recent past, that has a present relevance, often with 'just'.  ► adverbs
structures.example: My mother has broken her right leg. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple with an increasing range of adverbs in the normal mid position.
structures.example: This is a famous seafood restaurant, you know, I've always loved seafood. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple to refer to a state or period of time which is unlimited or indefinite.
structures.example: In spite of bad weather forecasts on TV, it has been a sunny, warm weekend. (Spain; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the question form with an increasing range of verbs.
structures.example: How has your family been? (Mexico; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form of the present perfect simple with 'still' to emphasise that something that was expected to happen continues not to happen.  ► adverbs
structures.example: I still haven't read the role but when I read it, I was very excited and I accepted Mr Brown's offer. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple with a superlative adjective to talk about a unique experience.  ► adjectives: superlatives
structures.example: This restaurant has the most delicious shrimps I have ever tasted. (Mexico; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the full negative forms with a wide range of verbs, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: Thus, you have not fulfilled your task with due care, as you have stated in your letter. (Austria; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present perfect simple to introduce news.
structures.example: A new shopping centre has opened in our town. (Russia; C2 MASTERY; 2005; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form prepositional phrases with a preposition and a noun phrase.
structures.example: When I have free time, I go to the park with my dog. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'just' to modify prepositions.
structures.example: It's just near the cinema. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Hindi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of simple (single-word) prepositions.
structures.example: I'm sending some flowers to you. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Romanian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of complex prepositions.
structures.example: We can meet in the park near to my house at 7.00 p.m. (A2 Spanish Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of simple (single-word) prepositions.
structures.example: Please return it by tomorrow morning. (A2 Hindi)

structures.can_do: Can form prepositional phrases using the '-ing' form of verbs as complements.
structures.example: I can help by bringing the sound box and bit box I am free at friday 7:30 pm. (Bangladesh; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Bengali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can end a 'wh-' question with a preposition, where the preposition is stranded from its complement.
structures.example: Who are you going with? (Philippines; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of simple (single word) prepositions.
structures.example: If it is raining, the rain enters through the holes in the roof and makes the house wet. (B1 Fulani)

structures.can_do: Can end a reported question clause and a relative clause with a preposition, where the preposition is stranded from its complement. ► Clauses: relative
structures.example: So this is the best festival I been to. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Albanian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use less frequent simple prepositions, often in a more formal, literary or business context.
structures.example: Suddenly the lights went out and a kind of silent screaming was heard throughout the whole dark room. (B2 German)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of complex prepositions.
structures.example: My parents weren't happy when they heard that I wanted to go to Croatia with my friends instead of flying to the USA. (B1 German)

structures.can_do: Can use less frequent complex prepositions, often in a more formal, literary or business context.
structures.example: It's unbelievable that this civilization that lived a long time ago could be so ahead of their time. (C1 Brazilian Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use adverbs of degree to modify prepositions and prepositional phrases.
structures.example: It's quite near my house so I can go there easily. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use preposition + relative pronoun as complement, to avoid preposition stranding, often in formal contexts. ► Clauses: relative
structures.example: According to your advertisement in a language magazine, you have a vacancy in which I am very interested. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of complex prepositions.
structures.example: She did not say very much except for "oh" and "yes, yes" every once in a while. (B2 Dutch)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form.
structures.example: I am sending you some flowers, because you are not well. (Bengali, A1 BREAKTHROUGH, 2009)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form.
structures.example: [talking about a computer] I’m not using it any more. (A2 Turkish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with an increasing range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.
structures.example: I am watching a swimming competition. (A2 Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.
structures.example: [in a message to someone who is ill] We are missing you. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Nepali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of verbs to talk about temporary situations.
structures.example: [talking about a temporary situation] I'm living with my friend in Wolverhampton. I'm studying at Wolverhampton College. (A2 Arabic - European)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-' questions, especially in the context of letters and emails.
structures.example: Dear Mom, How are you doing? (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Thai; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous to describe temporary actions which are repeated or regular.
structures.example: I'm doing a lot of great leisure activities. (B1 Catalan)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a limited range of adverbs of indefinite frequency, often to talk about surprising or undesirable situations or events (especially with 'always').
structures.example: I'm always dreaming about a job as a secretary. (A2, Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a wide range of verbs to talk about temporary situations.
structures.example: I'm enjoying a sunny day, much better than England. (B1 Chinese)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a wide range of verbs to talk about situations and events in progress.
structures.example: I’m planning a picnic on Saturday in the park. (Serbian, Yugoslavia, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2009)

structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with verbs that are not usually used in this form to make statements and requests sound less direct.
structures.example: Considering the importance of the matter, I am asking for your financial support. (Greek, Greece, C2 MASTERY, Pass, 2001)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with a wide range of adverbs of indefinite frequency, often to talk about surprising or undesirable situations or events.
structures.example: … we are persistently asking ourselves questions about where we are from and why we are here. (C2, Russian)

structures.can_do: Can use question forms to ask rhetorical questions.
structures.example: [writing about fashion] Are we becoming shallow? (C1 Czech)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
structures.can_do: Can use the present continuous with an increasing range of adverbs of indefinite frequency, often to talk about surprising or undesirable situations or events.
structures.example: … scientists don't really get together with top models … they are constantly studying and reading books, whereas the job of a top model is actually based on physical appearance. (B2 French)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with an increasing range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: They are very important to me, because they bring me good luck. (Key English Test, A2,Bulgarian)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: REAL AND IMAGINED SITUATIONS AFTER 'IF'
structures.can_do: Can use the present simple after 'if' to talk about real and imagined situations.
structures.example: If you want some help, I will be free next week. (Key English Test, A2, French)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: I don't like meat and fish. (Skills for life Elementary 1, A1, Kurdish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple to talk about repeated events or habits, and general facts.
structures.example: I work in a supermarket. (Skills for life Elementary 1, A1, Russian)

structures.can_do: Can use the affirmative form with a limited range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: Every day at college I learn new words and new things. (Skills for life Elementary 1, A1, Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with the adverb 'really' as an intensifier. ► adverbs
structures.example: I really like my kitchen, because it is big and new and it makes my cooking easy. (Skills for life Elementary 1; A1, Somali)

structures.can_do: Can use 'don't you think' or 'don't you agree' to look for agreement or an opinion.
structures.example: It's a bit strange, don't you think? (Preliminary English Test, B1, Spanish – Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with a wide range of subjects.
structures.example: Does your brother go with your parents? (Preliminary English Test, B1, German)

structures.guideword: FORM: WITH ADVERBS OF INDEFINITE FREQUENCY
structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with adverbs of indefinite frequency.    ► adverbs
structures.example: People usually try to eat their breakfast between 7 and 9 am. (Skills for Life Elementary 2, A2, Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'you'.
structures.example: Do you have a mobile phone? (Key English Test, A2, Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative form with an increasing range of regular and irregular verbs.
structures.example: I don't need the video because I've got the DVD. (Key English Test, A2, Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with a limited range of mental process verbs including 'think', 'hope', 'know'.
structures.example: I think my bag is in your kitchen. (Key English Test, A2,German)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with 'why don't you…?', 'Why don’t we…?' and 'if you want or if you like' to make suggestions.
structures.example: Why don't you wear your black suit? (Key English Test, A2, Arabic – Levant)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with an increasing a range of mental process verbs, including 'remember', 'understand', 'believe'.
structures.example: I'm reading an adventure book, I don't remember the title but it's very boring! (Preliminary English Test, B1, Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple to give instructions and directions.
structures.example: Then you turn right and my house is on your left. (Key English Test, A2, Greek)

structures.can_do: Can form indirect questions with 'Do you know' + 'how', 'where', 'why', or 'what …?'
structures.example: Do you know how to get to my house? (Key English Test, A2, Spanish)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with a limited range of speech act verbs, including 'suggest', 'apologise', 'recommend'.
structures.example: I suggest that if you travel, you should pay for your trip. (B1, Spanish – Latin American)

structures.guideword: FORM: INVERSION WITH 'NOT ONLY … BUT ALSO'
structures.can_do: Can use the inverted form of the past simple with auxiliary 'do', in the phrase 'not only … but also'.
structures.example: Not only do they save you filing time, but also they save office space. (First Certificate in English, B2, Chinese)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative question form as a persuasion strategy.
structures.example: Don't you just hate taking the bus to school every morning? well I have a perfect solution for you, a great bike with good brakes, a bell and lights. it is a great bike but since I never use it I would be happy to sell it to you. (Netherlands; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Dutch; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple to summarise events or plot in a story or piece of history, often to give immediate dramatic interest.
structures.example: The plot of the book takes place in Vienna after the Second World War. (First Certificate in English, B2, German)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with a limited range of reporting verbs, including 'say', 'show'.
structures.example: For example, I know a person that moved to my city two years ago, and now he says that it improved his social life. (Preliminary English Test, B1, Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with a wide range of speech act verbs, including '(dis)agree', 'accept', 'advise'.
structures.example: We disagree with the new numbering system as it is too complicated. (B2, Swiss German)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple with a wide range of reporting verbs, especially in academic contexts, including 'demonstrate', 'illustrate'.
structures.example: The popularity of this TV game in Russia clearly demonstrates the nature of human fears and dreams. (Certificate in Advanced English, C1, Russian)

structures.can_do: Can use the negative question form to check opinions.
structures.example: Doesn’t it sound fascinating? (Certificate in Advanced English, C1, Korean)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine' after 'of' in the phrases 'a friend of mine' and 'friends of mine'.
structures.example: A friend of mine gave me a present for my birthday. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours', with singular reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: It was my best present, although I also loved yours. (Key English Test; A2; Spanish-European)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'mine', with singular and plural reference, in subject and object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: I bought a new jacket because mine was very old. (Key English Test; A2; Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours' after noun + 'of'.
structures.example: Maybe you can take a friend of yours with you there. (Preliminary English Test; B1; German)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'ours' with singular and plural reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: Can we rent windsurf boards or should we bring ours with us? (First Certificate in English; B2; Turkish)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronouns 'hers' and 'ours' in comparative clauses.
structures.example: I told my mother that your Spanish omelette is better than hers. (First Certificate in English; B2; Spanish – European)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'ours' after noun + 'of'.
structures.example: Finally we went to Venice where we met some friends of ours and spent with them the rest of the holiday. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'ours', with singular and plural reference, in subject position.
structures.example: Ours is the only store in this locality which opens at 7.00 am. (Business English Certificate (Vantage); B2; Tamil)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'hers', with singular reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: At the entrance, the security guard asked for my identity card. Pat gave hers. (First Certificate in English; B2; French)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronouns 'mine' and 'yours', with singular reference, in comparative clauses after '(not) as … as'.
structures.example: Hope you have a friend as good as mine! (Preliminary English Test for Schools; Malaysia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'yours', with singular reference, in subject position.
structures.example: We bought it because yours is very old and sometimes stops working. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'ours', in subject position.
structures.example: I hope that other councils will consider improving the cyclists' cycling conditions as ours did. (Skills for Life; L2; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2007; Arabic - Other; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that … of' + possessive pronouns to express an attitude about someone or something, often in humorous or sarcastic contexts.
structures.example: I could just imagine it, meeting her at her house, her mother asking me to take care of her between puffs of smoke and coughing fits in that hoarse voice of hers. (Certificate of Proficiency in English; C2; Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'theirs', with singular and plural reference, in object positions, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: I could show them the traditional things of our country and learn theirs. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of singular reflexive pronouns ('myself', 'yourself') with a limited range of verbs ('enjoy', 'buy') to refer to actions where the subject and object of the verb are the same.
structures.example: I enjoyed myself so much. (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'his', with singular and plural reference, in subject and object position, and complement positions after 'be' and after prepositions.
structures.example: Therefore, his was not a happy and normal childhood. (C2 MASTERY; 1993; Spanish - Other; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'theirs', with singular and plural reference, in subject position.
structures.example: Theirs is a relationship between two members of the privileged classes, who really don't care about the world around (or below) them. (Portugal; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronoun 'hers' with singular reference, in subject position.
structures.example: I put Sophie's pictures in my bag because hers was already packed. (Certificate of Proficiency in English; C2; French)

structures.guideword: FORM: SAME SUBJECT AND OBJECT, SINGULAR
structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of singular reflexive pronouns with an increasing range of verbs to refer to actions where the subject and object of the verb are the same.
structures.example: I decided to talk to him and introduce myself. (Preliminary English Test; B1; Turkish)

structures.can_do: Can use the singular reflexive pronouns 'myself', 'yourself', 'himself' and 'herself' with 'by' to mean alone, without any help.
structures.example: I will ask my friends from the class and I will study by myself. (Preliminary English Test; B1; Czech)

structures.can_do: Can use the possessive pronouns 'hers', 'theirs' and 'his' after noun + 'of'.
structures.example: I was a great admirer of hers. (Certificate of Proficiency in English; C2; Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use the singular reflexive pronouns 'myself', 'yourself', 'himself' and 'herself' after prepositions where the object of the preposition is the same as the subject of the verb.
structures.example: He told me about himself and how he started playing the guitar. (Preliminary English Test; B1; Catalan)

structures.can_do: Can use the singular reflexive pronouns 'myself', 'yourself', 'himself' and 'herself' for emphasis.
structures.example: The best solution will be if you decide yourself what to do. (Preliminary English Test; B1; Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use plural reflexive pronouns with 'by' to mean alone, without any help.
structures.example: A friend of mine and I are planning to spend a short holiday by ourselves. (First Certificate in English; B2; Chinese)

structures.can_do: Can use the plural reflexive pronoun 'yourselves' for politeness.
structures.example: Dear Sir/Madam, I am writing to you in response to the advertisement published by yourselves in "the Traveller" regarding The Trip of a Lifetime. (First Certificate in English; B2; Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the singular pronoun 'itself' for emphasis.
structures.example: In my opinion, the main characters do not have to be liked by readers but the story itself must be good and interesting to be successful. (First Certificate in English; B2; Swiss German)

structures.can_do: Can use plural reflexive pronouns after prepositions where the object of the preposition is the same as the subject of the verb.
structures.example: Doing sports is an excellent way to relax and it can help us to feel good about ourselves. (First Certificate in English; B2; Hungarian)

structures.guideword: FORM: SAME SUBJECT AND OBJECT, PLURAL
structures.can_do: Can use plural reflexive pronouns to refer to actions where the subject and object of the verb are the same.
structures.example: In this way we will be able to enjoy ourselves even if this is not well-paid work. (First Certificate in English; B2; Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use plural reflexive pronouns for emphasis.
structures.example: The food is not very good, but sometimes we can prepare something to eat ourselves. (First Certificate in English; B2; Czech)

structures.can_do: Can use the reflexive pronoun 'itself' with 'by' to mean alone or without any help.
structures.example: If an animal is kept by itself , with no one to keep it company, it will get lonely and very sad. (First Certificate in English; B2; Danish)

structures.can_do: Can use the fixed expression 'in itself' as an intensifier .
structures.example: I would also spend much more quality time with my family as a whole, which is quite important in itself. (First Certificate in English; B2; Spanish _ Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronouns 'you' and 'it' after 'be' in question forms.
structures.example: Hi, Mrs. Bishop. How are you? (Skills for Life (Entry 1); ; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronoun 'it' as a direct object to refer to an object or situation already referred to.
structures.example: The maths is boring and I don't like it. (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use the object pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'it', 'us' and 'them' in the object position after prepositions.
structures.example: I really like to learn new words. It's very important for me. (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use 'as for myself' as a discourse marker to introduce or focus on a personal opinion.
structures.example: As for myself, as you can clearly see from my account of this musical event, music still means an awful lot to me, and most probably allways will. (Belgium; C2 MASTERY; 2001; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'we' and 'they' after an auxiliary or modal verb in question forms.
structures.example: Can I help you? (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; Arabic – other)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronouns 'me', 'you', 'him', 'her', 'us' and 'them' in the direct object position after a transitive verb.
structures.example: I'm very happy that you want to see me. (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; German)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronoun 'it' before 'be' to refer to a first person speaker or writer.
structures.example: Hello Mrs Bishop. It's Clarisse (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; French)

structures.can_do: Can use the pronouns 'I', 'you', 'he', 'she', 'it', 'we' and 'they' in the subject position before a verb in statements.
structures.example: In my free time I go shopping and I like swimming. (Skills for Life (Entry 1); A1; Polish)

structures.can_do: Can leave out the subject pronoun with 'hope'. ► ellipsis
structures.example: Hope to see you soon. (Key English Test ; A2; Turkish)

structures.can_do: Can use 'it' as an empty subject when there is nothing else to put in subject position, particularly with weather or time.
structures.example: It's warm and windy. (Key English Test for Schools; A2; Vietnamese)

structures.can_do: Can use 'it' as an object with 'make' to introduce something the speaker or writer is going to refer to.
structures.example: This shyness makes it hard for me to speak in public, or even to go out with my friends as often as I should. (First Certificate in English; B2; Spanish – European)

structures.can_do: Can leave out the subject pronoun with a limited range of verbs, in informal contexts. ► ellipsis
structures.example: Must rush now because I have to go out with Paul. (First Certificate in English; B2; Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use 'one' as a generic personal pronoun in the subject position to mean people in general. ► generic pronouns
structures.example: If one doesn't live close enough to walk to work, one can choose to get there by bicycle or by car. (First Certificate in English; B2; Swedish)

structures.can_do: Can use dummy 'it' with 'appears', 'feels', 'looks' and 'seems'.
structures.example: When you watch a film, it seems to be that you are inside it, and you are a character in it. (First Certificate in English; B2; Spanish - Latin American)

structures.can_do: Can use dummy 'it' as a subject to introduce something the speaker or writer is going to refer to.
structures.example: It is best to spend your time in the countryside. (Preliminary English Test ; B1; Chinese)

structures.can_do: Can use 'it' with the passive voice where the subject is unknown or unimportant, often in formal contexts. ► passives
structures.example: It was considered to be the most important thing to supply every computer with Internet and E-mail access (Certificate in Advanced English; C1; German)

structures.can_do: Can form a cleft construction beginning with 'it' to emphasise the subject of the main clause. ► clauses
structures.example: It was my father who took all this away from me. (Certificate of Proficiency in English; C2; Greek)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this' as a pronoun with singular reference.
structures.example: This is a very interesting place. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Panjabi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to refer back to single things or groups of plural things which have already been mentioned.
structures.example: Thank you for this. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to point to or identify single things or entities which are about to follow and have immediate relevance.
structures.example: This is my number: 0754 567 78 51. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that' as a pronoun to refer back to something which has already been mentioned.
structures.example: You know that blue is my favourite colour, so we are going to use that. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Tamil; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that's' + adjective to respond to something.
structures.example: That's great! (Switzerland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that' as a pronoun with singular reference.
structures.example: That was amazing. (Peru; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to refer to something that is happening now.
structures.example: This is the best holiday I have ever had! (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this' as a pronoun to refer back to whole clauses or sentences, especially to highlight or continue an important topic.

structures.can_do: Can use 'those' as a pronoun with plural reference.  ►  noun phrases
structures.example: Most of my clothes are lemon, green or orange, those are my favourite colours! (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'those' as a pronoun to refer to things which have already been mentioned.  ►  noun phrases
structures.example: Those are the things I like the most about her. (Chile; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that's all' to end a letter.
structures.example: That's all for now. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'these' as a pronoun with plural reference.  ►  noun phrases
structures.example: These are the most important years for us as teenagers, and they have to be the best years! (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'these' as a pronoun to refer to something with immediate relevance which has already been mentioned.  ►  noun phrases  ►  pronouns: demonstrative
structures.example: He is very clever and generous, and these are the things that I like most about him. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this one', 'that one' as a substitute for countable singular nouns that have previously been mentioned.
structures.example: I don't usually wear dresses but I had to buy this one because I am going to be in a singing competition. (Thailand; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Thai; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use quantifying determiners + 'of' with demonstrative pronouns  ► determiners: demonstrative
structures.example: If you can't, you must choose one of these. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'that of' and 'those of' as a possessive form, in formal and professional contexts.
structures.example: It is widely known that the Russian educational system differs dramatically from that of the European, Asian or American countries. (Russia; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'those' as a substitute, followed by a relative clause or '-ed' or '-ing'.
structures.example: Moreover, for those who are not interested in sports and who prefer shopping, it would be a good idea to prevent cars and especially lorries from running in the center of the town. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of pronouns ('all', 'both') with 'of' followed by an object pronoun, to refer to quantity.
structures.example: There are a lot of functions but I don't know how to use all of them. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use pronouns 'some' and 'any', to refer to quantity.
structures.example: [talking about items of clothing] Some were cheap but some were expensive. (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'these ones', 'those ones' as a substitute for plural countable nouns that have previously been mentioned.
structures.example: This is only the beginning; there are a lot of things that should be done, but let's just start with these ones. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'some' as a subject and object to refer back to a plural or uncountable noun.
structures.example: I saw a lot of people on the beach, some were playing football and some were sunbathing. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2011; Somali; Pass

structures.guideword: FORM: SUBJECT AND OBJECT PRONOUNS, 'BOTH', 'A FEW', 'ANOTHER'
structures.can_do: Can use 'both', 'a few', 'another' as subject and object pronouns.
structures.example: [talking about two types of exercise] Both are going to keep you fit. (Greece; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'any' as an object in a negative clause to refer back to a plural or uncountable noun.
structures.example: Bring some good CDs. I don't have any. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use pronouns 'each', 'either', 'enough', 'neither', 'several' as subject and object pronouns.
structures.example: As you could guess, each has a very unique style. (Korea, South; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Korean; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of pronouns ('neither', 'either', 'none') with 'of' followed by an object pronoun.
structures.example: Stella and her boyfriend, ... lived with Chuck at the same house, but neither of them knew that Chuck had passed a very complicated exam to be a spy for the United States. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of pronouns ('some', 'a few', 'any', 'each') with 'of' followed by an object pronoun.
structures.example: Of course some of them are closer than others but I love them all. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use pronouns 'none' to substitute for subject and object pronouns. ►  pronouns: substitution
structures.example: As for disadvantages, in fact, I see none. (Russia; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Russian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'few', 'many', 'most', 'others' to refer to people in formal written contexts, often reports or surveys.
structures.example: Few people stop to think about what they are really doing, and few are motivated to work at all. (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'some of', 'many of' to modify relative pronouns in a relative clause.
structures.example: The people of his time were amazed every time they saw his new inventions, some of which were enormous. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can modify 'few' and 'many' with 'very', 'too', 'so' as intensifiers.
structures.example: It was on Thursday that I realized how many children were in the centre. There were too many and the day was extremely tiring. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'a lot' and 'much' as a subject pronouns. ► focus
structures.example: A lot has changed since prehistoric times. (Netherlands; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Dutch; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: 'MANY ARE THE' + NOUN, FOR FOCUS
structures.can_do: Can form complex noun phrases using an inverted form 'Many' + 'are' + noun phrase, followed by a relative clause, as a focusing device.  ► focus
structures.example: Many are the causes which have led us to a better and longer life. (Spain; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'one' as a pronoun to substitute for singular countable nouns which have already been mentioned or are obvious from the context.
structures.example: [talking about a phone] I chose the black one with the numbers in orange. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'the one' and 'the' + pre-modifier + 'one' with a complement, to refer to something specific.
structures.example: My house is No.8 and it's the one with silver gates. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use determiners + premodifers + 'one'.
structures.example: I like my present very much because I needed a new one. (Netherlands; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Flemish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'this one', 'that one' to refer to a singular countable noun.  ►  pronouns: demonstratives
structures.example: I met many old friends there, because I was in another judo club before this one and my friends and I left the old one to join the 1.JCF, because we heard that this one is the best in the whole of Frankfurt. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'one' after 'which' in indirect questions to refer to one of two or more options.
structures.example: If you ask me which one I would choose, I would first go camping and then to Disneyland in Paris. (Ukraine; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'ones' as a pronoun to substitute for plural nouns which have already been mentioned or are obvious from the context.
structures.example: My pillows are getting old and I need new ones. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'these ones', 'those ones' as a substitute for plural countable nouns which have already been mentioned or are obvious from the context.
structures.example: This is only the beginning; there are a lot of things that should be done, but let's just start with these ones. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use premodifiers with 'ones', to refer to something in general.
structures.example: Our computers are out-dated and slow. I think we should replace them with new ones. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use determiners + premodifers + 'ones'.
structures.example: We should buy some new copiers and some new faxes because the old ones are very slow, and one copier is already broken. (Austria; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'none' as a pronoun. ►  determiners: quantity  ►  pronouns: quantity
structures.example: Then I searched for a Coca-Cola, but I found none. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'the ones' with a complement, to refer to something specific.
structures.example: Weddings in our country? Well, they're pretty different from the ones in England. (Yugoslavia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Serbian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns as objects or complements of prepositions.
structures.example: [talking about a phone] I need it because I have to call someone. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of indefinite pronouns as objects.
structures.example: I like doing everything at College because I love my college … (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Arabic - Other; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'The one(s) that' + clause in subject position, for focus. ► focus
structures.example: The one that impressed me a lot is the Chinese Lunar New Year Carnival which was held in Hong Kong in January this year. (Hong Kong; C2 MASTERY; 1998; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'everything' as subject, with a singular verb.
structures.example: I hope everything is all right. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of indefinite pronouns ('someone', 'everyone') as subjects, with a singular verb.
structures.example: I bought them because someone stole my luggage at the airport. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'something' in vague expressions, to refer to things in a non-specific way.
structures.example: After the concert we can have a pizza or something else. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can modify 'something' or 'anything' with an adjective, to make it more specific.
structures.example: Next weekend it's my mum's birthday party, so I needed something new to wear. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'anything' after a negative verb form.
structures.example: You don't have to bring anything. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use indefinite pronouns with 'else'.
structures.example: Have you got something else to do on Saturday or can you come with me? (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can modify 'something' or 'anything' with 'to' infinitive, to make it more specific.
structures.example: Please, bring something to drink. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of indefinite pronouns as objects or complements.
structures.example: I often watch TV, because my computer is broken and I have nothing to do. (Georgia (Republic of); B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Georgian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of indefinite pronouns ('something', 'nobody') as subjects, with a singular verb.
structures.example: I was so confused that I thought something was happening. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use indefinite pronouns with a relative clause to form complex noun phrases, to give focus.
structures.example: Something that I like very much is the idea of the classes. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2004; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'one' to refer to people in general, in formal contexts.
structures.example: The television, I think, is like a box where one can find anything: rubbish and good things. (Italian, B1 THRESHOLD, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use 'anything' in an ellipted clause, ('if there is anything …').
structures.example: Anything else you need, ask Sarah. (Portugal; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'you' to refer to people in general.
structures.example: My new mobile phone can do lots of things! You can play games, you can take pictures. (Turkish, A2 WAYSTAGE, Pass, 2007)

structures.can_do: Can use premodifiers with indefinite pronouns, often to intensify.
structures.example: You can find absolutely anything, whatever you need. (Kazakhstan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Kazakh; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'anything' with post-modifiers to form complex noun phrases as subjects with a singular verb, to give focus.
structures.example: Anything else can be attached too if needed. (China; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the full range of indefinite pronouns as subjects, with a singular verb.
structures.example: But, nowadays nothing is free, so you have to pay for everything. (Hungary; B2 VANTAGE; 2002; Hungarian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use indefinite pronouns in vague expressions to refer to things in a non-specific way.
structures.example: Is it worth having a nervous breakdown or anything like that? (Portuguese, B2 VANTAGE, Pass, 1993 )

structures.can_do: Can use 'we' and 'us' to refer to people in general.
structures.example: These days the car is everywhere, we can see cars all over the world. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'they/them' to refer back to indefinite pronouns when we do not know the number or gender.
structures.example: If someone is watching a film that they don't like they can always choose another channel to watch to. (Portugal; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use 'he/she', 'he' or 'she' or 'they' to refer back to gender neutral singular nouns or indefinite pronouns when we are not sure of the gender.
structures.example: If a child had free time, he/she would play on his/her own and not with other children. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2006; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'each other' as the object of a verb or complement of a preposition to talk about the mutual behaviour of two or more people.
structures.example: We go to the same school so we see each other every day. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'each' (+ noun or pronoun) as subject followed by 'the other(s)' a complement of a preposition, to refer to two related things. ► pronouns: quantity
structures.example: Each person could be a help to the other. (Sri Lanka; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; Tamil; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'one another' as the object of a verb or complement of a preposition to talk about the mutual behaviour of two or more people, often in formal contexts.
structures.example: I also thought to create a studying space where students, staff and visitors can meet one another. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'each' (+ noun or pronoun) as subject followed by 'the other(s)' as object , to refer to two related things. ► pronouns: quantity
structures.example: Each of them admires the other's intelligence. (Italy; C2 MASTERY; 1993; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative question with 'or something else' as the second alternative to a noun phrase, to refer to something non-specific.
structures.example: Shall we buy him a book, a CD or something else? (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions using 'or not' to substitute for a clause, sometimes to express annoyance or impatience.
structures.example: For a few seconds he was quiet. I couldn't wait, I asked nervously about his exam, did he pass or not? (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Polish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions with two phrases combined with 'or'.
structures.example: Is this area in the city or in the countryside? (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions with two words from the same class combined with 'or'.
structures.example: Can you bring some food or drinks for the dinner? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions with two clauses combined with 'or'.
structures.example: Are you still with him or did you two break up? (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions with two clauses and ellipsis in the second clause, often as a hedging device.
structures.example: Maybe you could hand out toys or show a movie? (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2005; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions using an extreme alternative to give greater pragmatic force.
structures.example: Is this new industry a blessing for the region or the exact opposite? (Netherlands; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2004; Dutch; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + AFFIRMATIVE QUESTION TAGS
structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of affirmative tags with affirmative clauses.
structures.example: Your boyfriend is also 16, is he? (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form alternative questions with two or more clauses and ellipsis in the second or third clause.
structures.example: Is it not better to take the television away or stop them going to the cinema? (Switzerland; C2 MASTERY; 1993; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of question tags.
structures.example: You don't know where I live, do you? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + NEGATIVE QUESTION TAGS
structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of 'be', 'do', 'have' and modal verb tags with negative main clauses.
structures.example: And so you're moving to a different area, aren't you? (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: NEGATIVE MAIN CLAUSES + AFFIRMATIVE QUESTION TAGS
structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of affirmative 'be', 'do' and 'have' tags with negative main clauses.
structures.example: I mean, your parents don't like discos, do they? (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: TAGS WITH IMPERATIVES AS SOFTENERS
structures.can_do: Can use an affirmative or negative tag after an imperative clause to soften the imperative.
structures.example: Think about it, will you? (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'right' as a tag in informal contexts.
structures.example: You are 14 years old, right? (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use affirmative and negative forms of question tags with 'there' + 'be'.
structures.example: As you put it that way, there isn't much of a difference with our time, is there? (Netherlands; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2000; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'have' to form 'wh-'questions. ► present perfect  ►  past perfect
structures.example: How have you been? (2666051_1; KET; Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions. ► present simple;  ► past simple
structures.example: What do you think? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2001; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + auxiliary 'be' to form 'wh-'questions. ► present continuous ► past continuous
structures.example: Who are you going with? (Philippines; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tagalog; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions.
structures.example: What will you bring? (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative question 'why don’t' + pronoun + verb, to make a suggestion or invitation.
structures.example: Why don't we watch a film? (Tamil, A2 WAYSTAGE)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + main verb 'be' + subject to form 'wh-' questions.
structures.example: How was your dinner yesterday? (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + the negative form of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions.
structures.example: Why can't you do both things? (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'questions as a focusing device, often in a narrative or argument.
structures.example: Nevertheless, we still give presents because we really want to. You can recognize them normally very fast! They are the ones which are unexpected and made with lots of love. So what makes a good present? From my point of view, the best presents are personal and fitted to the individual. (Germany; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2008; German; Pass

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.  ► can
structures.example: Can you come to dinner in my house? (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Polish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: NEGATIVE QUESTIONS WITH MAIN VERBS
structures.can_do: Can use 'wh-'words + the negative form of auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'wh-'questions.
structures.example: You still have this agonising headache. Why don't you go to your doctor? (Polish, B2 VANTAGE)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'be' + subject + the '-ing' form (continuous form) to form 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Are you going to come? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Catalan; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'do' + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: My favourite song is 'Viva la vida'. Do you know it? (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - European; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'have' + subject + the '-ed' form to form 'yes/no' questions.  ►  present perfect
structures.example: I've just watched a football competition with my family and friends. Have you watched it? (Japan; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use main verb 'be' + subject to form 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Are you ok? (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Kurdish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of modal verbs + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Could you meet me at my home at 7 pm? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use main verb 'be' + 'n’t' to form negative 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Aren't you excited about it? (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; ; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary 'do' and 'have' + 'n’t' + subject + main verb to form negative 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Don't you think so? (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use modal verbs + 'not' + subject + main verb to form 'yes/no' questions.
structures.example: Wouldn't you like to come? (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use negative 'yes/no' questions to involve the listener or reader by seeking agreement.
structures.example: Finally two days ago I found it in my pocket! It's funny! Don't you think? (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can form negative questions with uncontracted 'not' to emphasise a point in an argument.
structures.example: Do we not want our children to be as happy as possible? (Argentina; C2 MASTERY; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: REPORTED STATEMENTS WITH 'TELL', PRONOUN SHIFT
structures.can_do: Can report statements using a reporting clause with 'tell' + direct object + 'that-'clause, with a pronoun shift where relevant.
structures.example: [about a mobile phone] It's very important to me to have it with me because my brother is in the hospital and my father told me that he will call. (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report questions using 'ask' + 'if' or 'whether' + clause, with a pronoun and tense shift where relevant.
structures.example: You asked me if I like shopping. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; German; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: REPORTED STATEMENTS WITH 'SAY', PRONOUN SHIFT
structures.can_do: Can report statements using a reporting clause with 'say' + 'that-'clause, with a pronoun shift where relevant.
structures.example: My mother said that she can take us there. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report 'wh-'questions using a reporting verb + 'wh-'word + clause, with a change of pronoun and tense shift where relevant.
structures.example: I asked why she was here. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Italian; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: REPORTED STATEMENTS, PRONOUN AND TENSE SHIFT
structures.can_do: Can report statements using a reporting clause with 'say' or 'tell' + 'that-'clause, with a pronoun and tense shift where relevant.
structures.example: I immediately called her to see if everything was o.k. and she said that she had won the lottery and she wanted to give some of the money to me. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report speech about events in the future with and without backshifts for words relating to time.
structures.example: At the airport they told him to come the next morning. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report requests and commands with 'ask' or 'tell' + direct object and 'to-'infinitive.
structures.example: She asked me to come back as soon as possible because my father is seriously ill. (Malaysia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2005; Malay; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, END POSITION
structures.can_do: Can report speech and thought directly using the reporting verb after the reporting clause.
structures.example: “Excuse me Sir, but you forgot your mobile phone," she said. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, INITIAL POSITION
structures.can_do: Can report speech and thought directly, using the reporting verb before the reporting clause.
structures.example: He felt like a worm too and he said to me: "I'm sorry I'm not a good friend". (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2000; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report thought using 'wonder' + 'wh-'word + clause, with a tense shift where relevant.
structures.example: I always had good times with her and was very impatient to read this letter: I wondered what she had written. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can modify the reporting verb with an adverb.
structures.example: "So this is a real cow, mom?" she asked doubtfully. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, MID POSITION
structures.can_do: Can report speech and thought directly using the reporting verb in the mid position of the reported clause.
structures.example: "No problem", I thought, "there is only one person". (Botswana; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: DIRECT SPEECH, REPORTING CLAUSE, INVERTED SUBJECT
structures.can_do: Can report speech directly inverting the subject and verb in the reporting clause where the subject is a proper noun or noun phrase.
structures.example: "I was astonished when I saw them standing there", said John. (Netherlands; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Dutch; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the past continuous of the reporting verb to report mental processes, with a finite or non-finite 'wh-'clause in the reported clause.
structures.example: I was wondering why I failed. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use the present simple form of the reporting verb to report information from a written source and a present tense verb in the reported clause.
structures.example: First of all, your advertisement says that you have got two great nights in a hotel for us. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Turkish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: REPORTED REQUESTS AND COMMANDS, NEGATIVE
structures.can_do: Can report requests and commands with 'ask' or 'tell' + direct object + 'not' + 'to-'infinitive.
structures.example: Meanwhile, she told me not to be scared but the place was very... old. (Brazil; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can report speech about events in the past with backshifts for tenses and words relating to time.
structures.example: She had told me the previous day that she had something important to tell me. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'look forward to' as a fixed expression followed by an '-ing' form or noun phrase, usually at the end of correspondence.
structures.example: I'm looking forward to seeing you! (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of verb + particle + preposition + noun or pronoun.
structures.example: I can look up to someone in admiration if he (or she) is dedicating his (or her) life to helping other people. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 2005; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of verbs + particle + preposition + noun or pronoun.
structures.example: I could catch up with the work I miss after school from 3 to 4. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2006; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use verb + particle + preposition, where the preposition is separated from its complement. ► Prepositions
structures.example: Anyway, let me tell you what ideas I came up with. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an adverb between the verb and the preposition.
structures.example: I am really willing to know more about horses and to learn how to deal properly with them. (Brazil; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of verbs, typically reporting, with a 'that'-clause as the direct object.
structures.example: I hope that you'll come. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Tamil; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.
structures.example: If you need more information, please look at the information sheet at the entrance. (Switzerland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Swiss German; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of prepositional verbs followed by noun or pronoun objects.
structures.example: I listen to music in the living room, and also eat my breakfast, lunch and dinner. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Dari; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use verb + preposition, where the preposition is separated from its complement.
structures.example: In Poland rules that refer to how to dress at school aren't very strict; we don't wear any uniforms, but our clothes have to be clean and nice to look at. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 2000; Polish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: VERB + DIRECT OBJECT + PARTICLE + PREPOSITION + OBJECT
structures.can_do: Can use a direct object with some prepositional verbs as well as an object of the preposition.
structures.example: It is widely accepted that being a loyal and trusted individual means that the people around us can trust us or let us in on a secret. (Greece; C2 MASTERY; 2009; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use verbs, typically reporting verbs, followed by a noun or pronoun as the indirect object and a clause with or without 'that', as the direct object.
structures.example: I told you that she has a new car? (Peru; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: VERBS + DIRECT OBJECT CLAUSE WITHOUT 'THAT'
structures.can_do: Can use reporting verbs, especially mental process verbs, with a clause as the direct object, without 'that', especially in informal contexts.
structures.example: I hope you can go, buddy. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
structures.example: I heard about this club when I was watching T.V. and I wanted to check it out. (B1, French)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs + particle + object.
structures.example: Were it not for my university, I would give up this class immediately. (B1, Russian)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of verbs, typically reporting or mental process verbs, with a 'that'-clause as the direct object.
structures.example: Now you're sixteen, I totally understand that you don't want to go on holiday with your parents. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs without an object.
structures.example: I'm going to get up early on Saturday. (A2, Portuguese)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs without an object.
structures.example: Some species are dying out, and keeping such animals in zoos where they can give life to new generations is the only way to prevent them from becoming completely extinct. (B2 Polish)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
structures.example: I will pick you up and arrange everything. (A2 Burmese)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of phrasal verbs without an object.
structures.example: I needed to hang out because my life was too jam-packed and hectic. (B1, Italian)

structures.can_do: Can use some reporting verbs with a prepositional phrase followed by a 'that'-clause as the direct object.
structures.example: I think also that you should say to your parents that you want to try a new experience with your friends. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary verb 'be'. ►  present continuous
structures.example: I am writing to tell you what I do every day at college. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Mandarin; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
structures.example: [talking about a band] I went to check them out last week and here is my review of the two concerts. (Denmark; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Danish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of modal auxiliary verbs ('can', 'will', 'would').
structures.example: Can you bring some music with you to the dinner. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Bengali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use phrasal verbs + nouns as object + particle.
structures.example: I am glad that you have decided to take some time off and more glad because you are going to the U.S. (Chile; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use linking verb 'be'.
structures.example: I am 22 years old. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Bengali; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs + particle + object.
structures.example: I don't need to use my imagination while I'm surfing the internet, but if I'm reading a book I can build up the whole surroundings and the characters in my own head. (B2, German)

structures.can_do: Can use regular and irregular main verbs in simple verb phrases. ► present simple ► past simple
structures.example: You know, I love your cooking! (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2006; Slovak; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of modal auxiliary verbs.
structures.example: And I think we should go somewhere else to have a drink after the film. (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Vietnamese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use linking verbs with adjective complements.
structures.example: It makes me feel comfortable and the room looks bigger with the colour. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Thai; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use auxiliary verbs 'have' and 'do'.
structures.example: It has been a long time since I saw you. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2003; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by a 'to'- infinitive.
structures.example: I like to go to the zoo. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Arabic - Other; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verbs, 'dare' and 'need'.
structures.example: You needn't worry about where we can stay. (China; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Chinese; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM: SEMI-MODAL AUXILIARY VERBS, 'USED TO', 'OUGHT TO'
structures.can_do: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verbs, 'used to' and 'ought to'.
structures.example: But we used to play together every single day! (Japan; B1 THRESHOLD; 1999; Japanese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use semi-modal auxiliary verb 'have (got) to'.
structures.example: You've got to bring paintbrushes, paper and paint, that's all. (Vietnam; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would like to' + infinitive.
structures.example: I would like to meet you to give you some information about the Brannl State and the shops near her. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Arabic - Other; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'like' followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.
structures.example: I like to work with my teacher. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use verbs expressing preference followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.
structures.example: I love to play football. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Thai; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'enjoy' followed by the '-ing' form.
structures.example: We enjoy playing the piano and singing together. (Iran; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Farsi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would love to' followed by the 'to'-infinitive to give emphasis.
structures.example: I'd love to do the concert. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of verbs followed by a 'to'-infinitive.
structures.example: I bought them because I hope to go to England this year and the weather isn't very good. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of verbs followed by a 'to-' infinitive.
structures.example: … it's one of the reasons I decided to change class. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; French; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by an '-ing' form.
structures.example: I would like to stay there a few years to finish studying and to have my own money to start thinking of travelling. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'make' and 'let' + infinitive without 'to'.
structures.example: Let me know if it is suitable for you. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Portuguese; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would prefer' + 'to' infinitive, often for politeness.
structures.example: I would prefer to pay by cash. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'help' + object + infinitive with or without 'to', with no change in meaning.
structures.example: I wanted to help him to make some friends. He's just like me. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can introduce a new subject before the '-ing' form (using noun or object pronoun).
Can use some verbs of requesting and commanding followed by a direct object and a 'to-'infinitive.
structures.example: I would like you to come to a picnic on Saturday. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can follow some verbs with a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with a change in meaning.
structures.example: He said if you need to change the time, remember to contact him to make a new appointment. (Malaysia; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of verbs followed by an '-ing' form.
structures.example: [talking about cars] ... we can't avoid using them because we are used to them. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use some verbs connected with the senses + direct object + an '-ing' form, to give emphasis to an ongoing activity.
structures.example: Then I heard someone screaming, I was afraid and I said to the others: "Let's go out, something is happening". (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'there is' + singular noun phrase as complement.
structures.example: My home is nice, there is a nice garden. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

structures.guideword: FORM/USE: VERBS OF SENSES + OBJECT + INFINITIVE
structures.can_do: Can use some verbs connected with the senses + direct object + infinitive without 'to' emphasising a complete action.
structures.example: I would like to see it develop without any pollution and without destroying the environment. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Greek; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use 'there are' + plural noun phrase as complement.
structures.example: There are two bathrooms. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2009; Farsi; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'would hate' + 'to' infinitive, for emphasis.
structures.example: We in the student committee would hate to see all that space go to waste. (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2001; Swedish; Fail)

structures.can_do: Can use linking verb 'be' with complements.
structures.example: Because today is my birthday. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Mandarin; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'there' with a range of modal verbs + 'be' + complement.
structures.example: [talking about 20 years in the future] There will be flying cars and buses, and big houses. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'there is' + uncountable nouns as complement.
structures.example: I need it because there is some money in it which I have to pay to someone. (India; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; Malayalam; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'there' with other verbs with modal meaning + 'be' + complement.
structures.example: I figured out that there had to be matches somewhere; Bob, who owned the cabin, had told me that it was well equipped. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use both 'there is' and 'there are' + 'a lot of' + plural noun.
structures.example: There's a lot of people there. (Portugal; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use 'There' + 'be' + 'n’t' with countable and uncountable nouns.
structures.example: There isn't any noise. (Peru; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use a wide range of linking verbs with complements.
structures.example: There are indeed many ways of doing this and it all seems very confusing. (Denmark; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Danish; Pass)

structures.can_do: Can use an increasing range of linking verbs with complements.
structures.example: It looks good on you. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)
